stories.headline: Trumbull Household Hazardous Waste Collection returns Saturday, Oct. 3 at Indian Ledge
stories.summary: Trumbull, Monroe, and Easton residents can drop household hazardous waste Saturday, October 3, from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. at 307 Indian Ledge Park Drive next to the BMX facility — bring a Connecticut driver’s license. The town wants oil- and latex-based paints, solvents, pesticides (including restricted neonicotinoid products toxic to bees), pool chemicals, fluorescent bulbs, and mercury thermometers in original closed containers; do not mix chemicals. Asbestos, ammunition, medical sharps, propane tanks, and commercial waste are refused; tires, antifreeze, motor oil, and car batteries go instead to the TEaM Transfer Station on Spring Hill Road.

stories.headline: Apple’s October slate: iPhone Duo, iOS 27.1/27.2, 512GB Mac Studio — and rumored iPad mini 8
stories.summary: MacRumors maps a crowded Apple October: foldable iPhone Duo pre-orders Friday, Oct. 16 at 5 a.m. Pacific for an Oct. 23 launch; iOS 27.1 expected before Duo ships and iOS 27.2 later for five more Siri AI languages; plus the high-end Mac Studio with M5 Ultra and 512GB of RAM due late month. Rumored unveilings include an OLED iPad mini 8 with A20 Pro, refreshed HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K with Wi-Fi 7, M6 iMac and MacBook Pro options, and a new home hub that may run “homeOS.”

stories.headline: Trump airs taxpayer-funded ‘final battle’ TV ad ahead of Nov. 3 midterms
stories.summary: President Trump rolled another taxpayer-funded black-and-white TV spot during Sunday NFL games, warning of a “final battle” to demolish the deep state and cast out communists, Marxists, and fascists. The White House calls it an educational “public service announcement” because it does not urge a vote and Trump is not on the November ballot; Democrats and Public Citizen say it violates appropriations bans on propaganda and the Hatch Act. Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) said no public official should spend public money on private ads for themselves.

stories.headline: Penguins lock 22-man opening roster — five on IR ahead of Wednesday at Flyers
stories.summary: General manager Kyle Dubas finalized Pittsburgh’s 2026-27 opening roster Monday: 13 forwards, seven defensemen, and goaltenders Sergei Murashov and Arturs Silovs — 22 players total for Wednesday’s 7:30 p.m. opener at Philadelphia. Justin Brazeau, Ben Kindel, Blake Lizotte, Bryan Rust, and Ryan Graves are on injured reserve; Tristan Broz, Melvin Fernstrom, Oliver Okuliar, and Gabriel D’Aigle are injured non-roster. Sixteen of the 22 dressed last season; newcomers include Gustafsson, Lapierre, Robertson, Carlile, Korczak, and van Riemsdyk.

stories.headline: Jets’ Breece Hall week-to-week after MRI brings better-than-feared quad news
stories.summary: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported Monday that Jets running back Breece Hall is week-to-week with a quad injury after an MRI that delivered “good news” versus the longer timeline feared when he left Sunday’s Lions loss grabbing his outer thigh. He is not expected for Week 4 at Chicago, but may avoid injured reserve if New York thinks he can return inside four weeks. Braelon Allen figures to lead the backfield with Isaiah Davis also in the mix after mainly special-teams work.

stories.headline: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones Gen 2 get Auracast and LE Audio in beta firmware
stories.summary: Firmware 10.12.12 for Bose’s $449 QuietComfort Ultra Headphones Gen 2 adds Bluetooth LE Audio and Auracast as beta features — the first Bose headphones to join the broadcast-audio club already used by some Sony, JBL, Samsung, and Sennheiser gear. Auracast lets a phone, TV, or venue transmitter stream to many headphones at once for gate announcements, lectures, or quiet late-night TV. The update also improves wired USB audio balance for gaming chat and web-conferencing compatibility; Bose says the non-Ultra QC Headphones Gen 2 should get the beta next.

stories.headline: Lenovo’s 15-inch Googlebook opens preorders at $1,149.99 — $150 under earlier hints
stories.summary: Preorders opened Monday for Lenovo’s largest first-wave Googlebook at $1,149.99, $150 below the $1,299 starting price that had circulated. The 15-inch Chromebook-class machine packs an Intel Core Ultra 5 325, 16GB of RAM, 512GB of storage, and an HDMI port, and The Verge says units ship from October 4. It is the biggest of the first five Googlebook models aimed at Google’s refreshed laptop push.

stories.headline: Every 2026 Harley Softail now ships with cornering ABS and a Milwaukee-Eight 117
stories.summary: Harley-Davidson’s full 2026 Softail line — Street Bob, Fat Boy, Heritage Classic, Breakout, Low Rider S, and Low Rider ST — now carries the Rider Safety Enhancements suite that once stayed on tourers and CVOs: lean-sensitive ABS, traction control, drag-torque slip control, TPMS, ride modes, cruise, USB-C, and LCD gauges. Every Softail also runs the Milwaukee-Eight 117 in Muscle, Torque, or Classic tunes (up to 114 hp / 128 lb-ft on the Low Rider S/ST). Retro-leaning Deadwood and Solo Trim packages keep the bar-hopper look while the electronics ride underneath.

stories.headline: Great Smoky Mountains unseats Acadia as America’s top-ranked fall national park
stories.summary: A Sudoku Bliss study cited by OutKick ranks Great Smoky Mountains National Park first for fall travel with a 94.7 score versus Acadia’s 86.6, using September–November NPS visits (2021–2025) plus Google review signals. The Smokies logged nearly 19 million fall visits across those years to Acadia’s roughly 6.5 million; Shenandoah, Rocky Mountain, and Grand Teton round out the top five. Peak color in the Smokies runs mid-October into early November at lower elevations, but October is the park’s busiest month — expect Cades Cove, Kuwohi, and Roaring Fork congestion and try Foothills Parkway or early/late windows.

stories.headline: Anthrax drops Cursum Perficio — first full album in a decade — amid Maiden tour
stories.summary: Anthrax released Cursum Perficio, the thrash veterans’ first studio album in ten years, with 11 tracks spanning political thrash (“It’s For the Kids”), blastbeat-leaning metal (“The Edge of Perfection”), and AOR-tinged hard rock (“Everybody’s Got a Plan”), plus a title-track video starring London May. Charlie Benante has said it is not necessarily the final record; Scott Ian is less sure. The band is on Iron Maiden’s Run For Your Lives North American dates with Megadeth as the run winds down.
